P01.note: 'lifted from a tune the audience already knew' plus 'less as theft' points to quotation; reprise (repeating one's own material) is the near miss.

P02.note: Warmth lures insects that then pollinate in return, so courts; feeds is loosely defensible as energy supply, but warmth isn't food.

P03.note: Hidden repainted layers make the oil surface poor evidence of order; you need the contrast and the final sentence to reject mixed and physical.

P04.note: 'The tale seems to have taken shape decades later' gives myth; 'no report of such a panic' kills report.

P05.note: Lichens build the soil that later plants need; crowding is the near miss, since it is the mosses that shade out the lichens.

P06.note: The urban margin covers the rural loss, which is the textbook sense of subsidize.

P07.note: The details the contract left open were the painter's own domain (province); motive tempts because of 'what a painter himself valued'.

P08.note: The first sentence describes a free trial outright.

P09.note: Each parish defined the categories its own way, so they were local; the parish examples are needed to see it.

P10.note: The 'has no physical form' versus 'walked through and inspected' contrast gives tangible directly.

P11.note: The debts were not forgiven, while the date was planned and the release publicly announced, so it was a symbolic gesture; planning kills gamble and the public crier kills intrigue.

P12.note: Smaller plants with no attackers measure the cost (burden); futility is the near miss, rejected by 'pays off ... when attackers are actually present'.

P13.note: Start times of 7:30, 8:00 and 8:30 spell out stagger.

P14.note: 'The fine print' tells you to read the terms; one sentence is enough.

P15.note: Ceremonial duties with no proposing or voting power mean honorary; hereditary is killed by 'passed ... in turn' among the guilds.

P16.note: 'Could not have been dug by either town alone' plus the 'single fund' make joint obvious.

P17.note: Once the shutter opened the camera could not decide, so it ruled out (precluded) judgment for the exposure only; outpaced and modified are near misses.

P18.note: 'Without restricting them' plus the jump in participation gives sway.

P19.note: Outbreaks worst after rainy summers means wet summers fuel the fungus; embolden is the wrong register, and chill and drown run the wrong way.

P20.note: Breathlessness added in the fourth revision means it was deliberately constructed (rehearsed); the drafts finding is needed.

P21.note: 'No longer reached its former peak speed' defines throttle.

P22.note: The old units stayed in active use for decades (lingered); fishmongers' open quoting rules out lurked and hibernated, but languished is a near miss.

P23.note: Each animal used its own method; cultural is killed by 'even animals that had watched a neighbor ... used a method of their own'.

P24.note: 'Into bodies kilometers wide in a single collapse' gives assemble; fracture is killed by the contrast with shattering.

P25.note: Profit share growing with tenure, which is what a worker gives up by quitting, means stake; say and toehold are near misses.

P26.note: Net (overall resulting) is an uncommon sense; personal is killed by 'not a direct record of what the author wrote'.

P27.note: Remembered gifts and gossip over unreturned ones show obligation (indebtedness); haggling is killed by 'no one ever named its price'.

P28.note: The campaign used existing networks it already belonged to (harnessed); infiltrated is the near miss, rejected because the organizers were members.

P29.note: Assets exceeding everything owed defines solvent, set against a liquidity crisis; thriving tempts on the 'yet' contrast.

P30.note: The program still runs and is halted by a signal, so eyelessness is its expression; 'rather than the loss' kills abandonment and fossil.

P31.note: A few spring days and one band per year means episodic; the regular yearly pattern kills chaotic and anomalous.

P32.note: Size makes migration possible and warmth triggers it (catalyst); foundation and deadline are near misses that need the dam evidence to reject.

P33.note: Repeated identical copies fixed the spellings (hardened, an uncommon sense); 'one regional dialect' kills hybridized.

P34.note: Broad aims instead of precise orders gave governors latitude (leeway); jurisdiction is a near miss, since their formal authority did not change.

P35.note: Each basin systematically over-represents one environment, so its record is biased; 'many preserved in fine detail' kills damaged.

P36.note: 'Ten short visits ... than one all-day stay' gives turnover; supply is killed by 'neither the number of spaces'.

P37.note: The court moved on a regular circuit, so government was itinerant; intermittent is a near miss, rejected by the continuous issuing of writs.

P38.note: Once faces were visible, broad gesture was no longer needed (needless); noticeable and routine are near misses.

P39.note: 'The author had to find something for him to do' makes the subplots necessities; the 'less indulgences than' contrast rejects novelties.

P40.note: Reordering the stanzas so the poem ends elsewhere means redirected; 'changed almost no words' kills reworded and 'kept every line' kills padded.
